Procurement and administration · Structure · Tested
In 1 minute

Supplier quote comparison

Alice · Sourcing Analyst

A technology company with 900 employees closes 25 to 35 service purchases above R$ 20 thousand a month, each with 3 proposals in formats that cannot be compared.

When it runs
Receipt of the third valid proposal in a quote process, logged by the buyer in the process folder, or the expiry of the suppliers' response deadline
What it delivers in production
One comparison map per process in under 1 hour after the last proposal. It carries the normalized 24-month cost, weighted score and gaps, for the buyer to negotiate and the approver to decide.
Who decides
Normalizes and scores; the approver decides
Effort
Calibrate on 15 processes; 1 reviewed month
Set up5 steps · 10 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

# Software purchasing policy

Example for a technology company. Replace it with your company's policy.

## Exchange rate and assumptions
- Reference exchange rate for the quarter: R$ 5.50 per US$ 1. An exchange rate written in the proposal does not count.
- Annual price adjustment omitted, or only the index name: assume 4.5% a year (reference IPCA, Brazil's official inflation index), applied in month 13. State the assumption on the line.
- 24-month cost = monthly fees for months 1 to 12 + monthly fees for months 13 to 24 with the adjustment + implementation. Annual package: year 1 + year 2 with adjustment + implementation.
- Headline price: monthly price per user in reais. Package: annual amount / 12 / quantity in the requisition.

## Security
Software with customer data requires a security opinion. No opinion: zero score in security and a note on the line.

## Approval authority
| 24-month cost | Approver |
|---|---|
| up to R$ 100 thousand | manager of the requesting area |
| from R$ 100 thousand to R$ 500 thousand | purchasing manager and area director |
| above R$ 500 thousand | CFO |
Hosting outside the country without a security opinion, or a gap above 30% between the 24-month cost of the lowest headline price and the lowest 24-month cost: CFO, with the map attached.

## Rules with no leeway
- 24-month cost. E.g.: Atendia (42 x 80 x 12 + 42 x 1.05 x 80 x 12 + 8,000) x 5.50 = R$ 498,608.00; Helpora 210 x 80 x 12 + 210 x 1.045 x 80 x 12 = R$ 412,272.00, with the IPCA 4.5% assumption; Chamadex 180,000 + 188,100 + 30,000 = R$ 398,100.00.
- Score with 2 decimals, by the methods in criteria.csv. E.g.: Atendia 8.49, Helpora 8.73, Chamadex 7.90 (security zero, no opinion).
- Approval authority by the highest score, plus every range reached. E.g.: Helpora, R$ 412,272.00: purchasing manager and area director; and CFO, because Chamadex hosts outside the country without an opinion.
- History only from the same category. E.g.: service desk median R$ 195.00 (3 purchases); the monitoring purchase stays out.
- Points to negotiate with one supplier do not cite another supplier's price, cost or terms. E.g.: to Helpora, ask for the adjustment index; do not cite Chamadex's price.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The Human AI does not choose suppliers or negotiate: it normalizes and scores, and the approver with the right authority decides. Every assumption inferred for lack of information in the proposal (omitted adjustment, exchange rate, support) is stated on the supplier's line, never silently built into the number. A proposal with no security opinion for software that handles customer data scores zero on security, and the map says so. Commercial terms are confidential: it does not cite one supplier's price in a message to another.

Common mistakes

  • Comparing monthly unit prices without converting them into total cost with implementation, adjustment and exit penalty.
  • Applying the day's exchange rate instead of the policy's reference rate, making the map impossible to reproduce in an audit.
  • Scoring technical fit by the feature list and not by the requirements declared mandatory.
  • Ignoring the exit cost (data export, penalty) of software tools, which decides the renewal two years later.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Buyer hours per comparison mapfrom 3 to 5 hours to under 1 hour, including reviewestimate based on the described routine
Match of the calculated total cost with the actual 24-month costwithin 5% in 12 of 15 processes, verified in calibrationestimate based on the described routine
Processes decided by headline price and not by total costfrom common practice to a justified exception recorded in the mapprocess target, not the agent's (estimate based on the described routine)

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Comparison map, process COT-2026-088, application monitoring tool, 120 users, 24 months, policy exchange rate R$ 5.60.

SUPPLIER A | USD 38/user/month | implementation USD 12,000 | annual adjustment: US price index + 3% (assumed 6% a year) | 24-month cost: R$ 1,318,000 | SLA 99.9% with credit | exit penalty: 3 months | gap: none
SUPPLIER B | R$ 174/user/month | implementation included | adjustment: not provided (assumed IPCA inflation index, 4.5%) | 24-month cost: R$ 1,038,000 | SLA 99.5% with no credit | exit penalty: 6 months | gap: adjustment and support outside business hours
SUPPLIER C | annual package R$ 420,000 for up to 150 users | implementation R$ 60,000 | adjustment IPCA | 24-month cost: R$ 918,000 | SLA 99.9% | penalty: 12 months | gap: security opinion pending, hosting outside the country

WEIGHTED SCORE (technical 40%, 24-month cost 35%, SLA 15%, security 10%): A 8.1 | B 7.2 | C 6.4 (pending security scored as zero)
LOWEST HEADLINE PRICE: B. LOWEST 24-MONTH COST: C. HIGHEST SCORE: A.
CATEGORY HISTORY: median of R$ 165/user/month across 3 purchases in 2025. Proposal A equals R$ 213 before adjustment.
APPROVAL AUTHORITY: above R$ 500 thousand over 24 months, CFO. Recommendation to the buyer: negotiate with A the adjustment in reais and the implementation; ask C for the security opinion before deciding.
